The test image shows two tomato stems pulled from soil, displaying the stem base and root system. Key features:
- Brown/dark internal discoloration of stem tissue (pith/vascular)
- Damaged, brown roots
- Stems appear split longitudinally showing internal browning
- No visible white mycelium, sclerotia, or fungal growth

This points to a vascular wilt disease. Top candidates: **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**, **Verticillium_Wilt**, **Bacterial_Wilt**, **Southern_Blight**.

Now viewing one reference from each of 4 candidates:

The fourth reference image (Southern_Bacterial_Wilt root, Bugwood 5473711) is nearly identical to the test image (Bugwood 5473712) - both show tomato stems pulled from soil against a white background, with dark brown stem-base discoloration and brown fibrous root systems. These are sequential images from the same photo series.

Key matches:
- White background, plants pulled from soil showing stem+root
- Extensive brown/dark discoloration at stem base
- Brown, damaged fibrous roots
- Green upper stem transitioning to brown at soil line

The Southern_Bacterial_Wilt symptom description matches: "base of the plant shows brown cankers and root rot with vascular discoloration."
